beats.trigger: Build one agent per recurring workflow

beats.trigger: If one agent can produce what you need, use one.
beats.got: Start with one agent. Splitting adds coordination cost, like adding people to a project.

beats.trigger: A legal-policy agent shouldn't have customer-data access.
beats.got: Split agents when they need different access, dialect or stance. The access example is something my DPO would nod at.

beats.trigger: The synthesizer had three stances in front of it and could not choose.

beats.trigger: The stances bring the variety. The frame brings the choice.

beats.trigger: Could one prompt produce the same quality of output?
beats.got: Same point as before: try one prompt first.

beats.trigger: Helper agents in one session (the Phase 2 move).
beats.got: Sessions versus helper agents is a technical choice. I think it matters for IT, but it doesn't change what I'd decide.

beats.got: nothing new. 'Tool surface' is jargon I don't know.

beats.got: Handoffs lose information, between agents and between people. That is a true observation.

beats.trigger: jot three to five lines on what matters about your company's data
beats.got: Prepare for next time by writing what is sensitive in my company's data. That lands close to my worry about employee data.

beats.trigger: An agent that works across connected systems has access to those systems.
beats.got: The question to ask about any agent is what the worst thing is that it could do with its access. That is a good question for the leadership team.

beats.trigger: You're close to an agent system that cracks your crux.
beats.got: Keep building. I'm not that close, and I'm not sure I believe it.

take_homes: Split into several agents only when they need different access, dialect or stance. Otherwise one good prompt is enough, and every handoff loses something.
Give the AI a framework to choose with. Otherwise it averages the views and nobody decided anything. I've seen the same in leadership meetings.
Ask what the worst thing is that an agent could do with its access, and keep a human approval step before it acts in another system.

monday.move: Ask my HR business partners and the DPO what employee data any agent may touch. I'd use that question to decide whether to try an agent for the weekly people-metrics summary at all.
monday.who: Me, with one HR partner and the DPO
monday.stop_condition: If the DPO says employee data needs the works council first, I stop and start that conversation instead of building.
monday.blocker: Employee data in an AI tool needs the works council and the DPO, and I haven't asked either yet.

misconception.why: Nothing in the module said which roles go or stay. The 'one agent per recurring workflow' idea made me think about workflows rather than roles, but I still expect headcount questions to come first.

one_line: Good rule of thumb that you should try one agent first, and it was honest that you can't check the answer, but it was windows and prompts with hardly a word about the people who do this work today.
